subproblem.title: Θ ≥ 1 μ_V-a.e. in U from θ ≥ 1 and ApproxTangentAE (statement (1.1))
subproblem.statement: Assume ApproxTangentAE. Let n ≥ 1, ℓ ∈ ℕ, V a rectifiable n-varifold in E = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, U ⊆ E open, and suppose θ ≥ 1 μ_V-a.e. in U (V.MultiplicityGE 1 U). Then for μ_V-a.e. x ∈ U the density Θ(x) = lim_{ρ↓0} μ_V(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) exists (V.HasDensityAt x (V.density x)) and Θ(x) ≥ 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ApproxTangentAE → ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)), 0 < n → IsOpen U → V.MultiplicityGE 1 U → ∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, x ∈ U → V.HasDensityAt x (V.density x) ∧ 1 ≤ V.density x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}; Hⁿ = μHE[n]; for an admissible pair a = (M, θ), mk a = v(M, θ) and its weight is pairWeight n M θ = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density x ↦ ofReal θ(x); μ_V = V.weight; B_ρ(x) = closedBall x ρ; ω_n = omega n; V.HasDensityAt x t means μ_V(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → t as ρ ↓ 0 (filter 𝓝[>]0, with μ_V(·) read as a real number via Measure.real), and V.density x is limUnder (𝓝[>]0) of the same quotient. Source: Step 1, statement (1.1), of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, opening of §5: 'θ ≥ 1 μ_V-a.e. in U' gives Θ ≥ 1 μ_V-a.e. in U, where Θ = θ by ApproxTangentAE).

1. By V.MultiplicityGE 1 U there is an admissible pair a = (M, θ) with mk a = V and θ(x) ≥ 1 for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ U)-a.e. x.
2. Since V = mk a and the weight is defined by Quot.lift (which computes on mk a), μ_V = pairWeight n M θ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ). A measure with a density with respect to ν is absolutely continuous with respect to ν (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), so μ_V ≪ Hⁿ⌞M. Consequently every property that holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. also holds μ_V-a.e.
3. U is open, hence a Borel set. Therefore Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ U) = (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞U (restrict_restrict for the measurable set U), and the statement of step 1 is equivalent to: for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, x ∈ U ⇒ θ(x) ≥ 1 (ae_restrict_iff' for the measurable set U).
4. ApproxTangentAE applied to n > 0, ℓ and the pair a gives, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, (mk a).HasDensityAt x (θ(x)); as mk a = V, this says V.HasDensityAt x (θ(x)).
5. Let x be a point of the intersection of the two Hⁿ⌞M-full sets of steps 3 and 4, and suppose x ∈ U. Then V.HasDensityAt x (θ(x)). The filter 𝓝[>]0 on ℝ is nontrivial and ℝ is Hausdorff, so the limit is unique and limUnder returns it (Mathlib Tendsto.limUnder_eq): V.density x = θ(x). Hence V.HasDensityAt x (V.density x), and V.density x = θ(x) ≥ 1 by step 3.
6. So the implication 'x ∈ U ⇒ (V.HasDensityAt x (V.density x) ∧ 1 ≤ V.density x)' holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, and by step 2 it holds for μ_V-a.e. x. ∎
proof_key_steps: MultiplicityGE gives a pair a = (M, θ) with mk a = V and θ ≥ 1 Hⁿ-a.e. on M ∩ U
μ_V = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ is absolutely continuous w.r.t. Hⁿ⌞M
ApproxTangentAE gives HasDensityAt x (θ x) for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, so density x = θ x by uniqueness of limits
Combine on U (Borel) and transfer the Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. statement to μ_V-a.e.

audit.reason: The frozen definitions support every step: MultiplicityGE supplies the representative, withDensity transfers almost-everywhere statements, openness justifies restriction to U, and ApproxTangentAE plus limUnder uniqueness identifies the density. No structural or parent conclusion is assumed.

subproblem.title: Sobolev preliminaries: C¹ extension and integrability of the energy integrand
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and let V be a rectifiable n-varifold in E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} whose weight μ = μ_V is finite on compact sets and such that x ↦ p_{T_xV} is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Let U ⊆ E be open, H: E → E locally μ-integrable on U, and g: E → ℝ C¹ on U with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ U. Then g is C¹ on all of E, ∇^M g(x) = 0 for every x ∉ tsupport g, and both |∇^M g| and g|H| are μ-integrable.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (H : Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (g : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight → IsOpen U → LocallyIntegrableOn H U V.weight → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g U → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ tsupport g → V.tangentialGradient g x = 0) ∧ Integrable (fun x ↦ ‖V.tangentialGradient g x‖) V.weight ∧ Integrable (fun x ↦ g x * ‖H x‖) V.weight
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; B_ρ(ξ) = closedBall ξ ρ (closed ball); ω_n = omega n ∈ (0, ∞) for n ≥ 1 (Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ, which is open, nonempty and bounded); μ = μ_V = V.weight; p_x = (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection, the orthogonal projection onto T_xV, a continuous linear map with |p_x v| ≤ |v| (Mathlib Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le); ∇g(x) = gradient g x (0 where g is not differentiable); ∇^M g(x) = V.tangentialGradient g x = p_x(∇g(x)). All integrals ∫ are Bochner integrals (value 0 for non-integrable integrands), so integrability is checked wherever integrals are compared or split; ∫_{(a,b]} denotes the Lebesgue integral over the interval Ioc a b. Source: Step 1 (Preliminaries) of the parent proof of SobolevInequality (Simon Ch. 4, §5). Let K := tsupport g.

1. (g is C¹ on E.) Let x ∈ E. If x ∈ U, then U is a neighbourhood of x (U is open) and g is C¹ on U, so g is C¹ at x. If x ∉ U, then x ∉ K because K ⊆ U; K is closed, so g vanishes identically on the open neighbourhood E ∖ K of x, hence g agrees near x with the constant 0 and is C¹ at x. Being C¹ at every point, g is C¹ on E (Mathlib contDiff_iff_contDiffAt; the same statement is SimonGMT Chapter04.RectifiableVarifold.contDiff_of_tsupport_subset). In particular g and x ↦ ∇g(x) are continuous on E.
2. (∇^M g vanishes off K.) If x ∉ K, then g = 0 on a neighbourhood of x, so Dg(x) = 0, ∇g(x) = 0, and ∇^M g(x) = p_x(0) = 0. In particular ∇g also vanishes off K.
3. (Finiteness.) K is compact because g has compact support, so μ(K) < ∞ since μ is finite on compact sets. The continuous functions |g| and |∇g| vanish off the compact set K, so M_0 := sup_E |g| < ∞ and M_1 := sup_E |∇g| < ∞ (each is a maximum over K, or 0 if K = ∅).
4. (|∇^M g| ∈ L¹(μ).) The map x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis, x ↦ ∇g(x) is continuous, and evaluation (P, v) ↦ P v, L(E, E) × E → E, is continuous; therefore x ↦ ∇^M g(x) = p_x(∇g(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and so is x ↦ |∇^M g(x)|. By step 2 and |p_x v| ≤ |v|, |∇^M g(x)| ≤ M_1·1_K(x) for every x ∈ E. The function M_1·1_K is μ-integrable because μ(K) < ∞, so |∇^M g| is μ-integrable.
5. (g|H| ∈ L¹(μ).) H is locally μ-integrable on U and K is a compact subset of U, so H is μ-integrable on K (Mathlib LocallyIntegrableOn.integrableOn_compact_subset); hence |H| is μ-integrable on K. On K the function x ↦ g(x)|H(x)| is a.e. strongly measurable (continuous factor times a.e. strongly measurable factor) and bounded in absolute value by M_0|H|, hence μ-integrable on K. Off K, g = 0 and therefore g|H| = 0. A function that is integrable on K and vanishes off K is integrable on E, so g|H| ∈ L¹(μ).
6. Steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 are the four asserted conclusions: g ∈ C¹(E); ∇^M g(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport g; |∇^M g| ∈ L¹(μ); g|H| ∈ L¹(μ). ∎
proof_key_steps: g is C¹ at points of U (U open) and near points off tsupport g (g ≡ 0 there), hence C¹ on E
∇g and ∇^M g = p_x(∇g) vanish off the compact K = tsupport g, and μ(K) < ∞
∇^M g is μ-a.e. strongly measurable from (FV3) and continuity of ∇g, and |∇^M g| ≤ (sup|∇g|)·1_K, so it is integrable
H is integrable on the compact K ⊆ U; g|H| ≤ (sup|g|)|H| on K and vanishes off K, so it is integrable

audit.reason: The proposition exactly matches the hypotheses and four conclusions. The proof establishes global C¹ regularity, vanishing gradients off the compact support, measurable projection evaluation, and both integrability claims. It correctly permits signed g and requires no positive-dimension hypothesis.

subproblem.title: Corrected Simon Lemma 5.8 (good-radius calculus lemma, n ≥ 2)
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 2, F ∈ ℝ and f, k: ℝ → ℝ be nondecreasing on (0, ∞) with 0 ≤ f(τ) ≤ F and 0 ≤ k(τ) for τ > 0. Assume (a) s^{−n}f(s) ≤ r^{−n}f(r) + ∫_{(s,r]} τ^{−n}k(τ) dτ for all 0 < s ≤ r, and (b) for every η < 1 there are arbitrarily small s > 0 with s^{−n}f(s) > η (i.e. limsup_{s↓0} s^{−n}f(s) ≥ 1). Then F > 0 and there is r with 0 < r < 2F^{1/n} and f(5r) ≤ 5ⁿF^{1/n}k(r) (= ½·5ⁿr_0k(r) with r_0 = 2F^{1/n}).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f k : ℝ → ℝ) (F : ℝ), 2 ≤ n → MonotoneOn f (Ioi 0) → MonotoneOn k (Ioi 0) → (∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ → 0 ≤ f τ ∧ f τ ≤ F) → (∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ → 0 ≤ k τ) → (∀ s r : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ r → f s / s ^ n ≤ f r / r ^ n + ∫ τ in Ioc s r, k τ / τ ^ n) → (∀ η : ℝ, η < 1 → ∃ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), η < f s / s ^ n) → 0 < F ∧ ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ r < 2 * F ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ ∧ f (5 * r) ≤ 5 ^ n * F ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * k r
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. All functions are real valued on ℝ; ∫_{(a,b]} and ∫_a^b denote Lebesgue integrals over (a, b] and [a, b] (equal, and equal to the integral over (a, b), for integrable functions). Source: Step 2 of the parent proof, the corrected Lemma 5.8 of Simon Ch. 4. Documented correction: Simon's printed Lemma 5.8 is inconsistent (its lower bound 1 ≤ σ^{−n}f(σ) for all σ contradicts boundedness of f); it is replaced by this version (lower bound only along small radii, i.e. limsup_{s↓0} s^{−n}f(s) ≥ 1, finite-interval inequality, same good-radius conclusion), and n ≥ 2 is required. Here F is any upper bound of f on (0, ∞); the parent proof takes F = f_∞ = sup f, and its argument uses only f ≤ F and r_0^{−n}F = 2^{−n}.

1. (F > 0.) Apply (b) with η = 0: since the frequently-condition is non-vacuous, there is s > 0 with f(s)/sⁿ > 0, so F ≥ f(s) > 0.
2. Put r_0 := 2F^{1/n} > 0. Since F > 0, (F^{1/n})ⁿ = F (Mathlib Real.rpow_inv_natCast_pow), so r_0ⁿ = 2ⁿF, i.e. r_0^{−n}F = 2^{−n}, and 5ⁿF^{1/n} = ½·5ⁿr_0.
3. (Integrability.) For 0 < a ≤ b, a function that is nondecreasing on [a, b] is measurable and bounded there (between its values at a and b), and τ ↦ τ^{−n} is continuous on [a, b]. Hence τ ↦ τ^{−n}k(τ), τ ↦ τ^{−n}f(τ) and τ ↦ τ^{−n}f(5τ) (f(5·) is nondecreasing on (0, ∞)) are integrable on [a, b] (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable; for τ^{−n}k(τ) this is also SimonGMT Chapter04.intervalIntegrable_radiusQuotient_of_monotoneOn, axiom-clean). All integrals below are of such functions.
4. Suppose, for a contradiction, that the conclusion fails: for every r with 0 < r < r_0, f(5r) > 5ⁿF^{1/n}k(r) = ½·5ⁿr_0k(r), i.e. k(r) < (2/(5ⁿr_0))·f(5r).
5. By (b) with η = 2/3, and since (0, r_0) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>]0, there is s with 0 < s < r_0 and f(s)/sⁿ > 2/3.
6. Let S := sup{τ^{−n}f(τ) : τ ∈ [s, r_0]}. The set is nonempty and bounded above by s^{−n}F (because f ≤ F, F > 0 and τⁿ ≥ sⁿ), so S is a real number; S ≥ s^{−n}f(s) > 2/3, and S ≥ 0.
7. Fix s' ∈ [s, r_0]. Hypothesis (a) with the pair (s', r_0) and f(r_0) ≤ F give s'^{−n}f(s') ≤ r_0^{−n}F + ∫_{(s',r_0]} τ^{−n}k(τ) dτ = 2^{−n} + ∫_{s'}^{r_0} τ^{−n}k(τ) dτ.
8. By step 4, τ^{−n}k(τ) ≤ (2/(5ⁿr_0))·τ^{−n}f(5τ) for all τ ∈ [s', r_0) (the endpoint r_0 is a null set), so by step 3, ∫_{s'}^{r_0} τ^{−n}k(τ) dτ ≤ (2/(5ⁿr_0))∫_{s'}^{r_0} τ^{−n}f(5τ) dτ.
9. Substituting u = 5τ (τ^{−n} = 5ⁿu^{−n}, dτ = du/5; Mathlib intervalIntegral.integral_comp_mul_left): ∫_{s'}^{r_0} τ^{−n}f(5τ) dτ = 5^{n−1}∫_{5s'}^{5r_0} u^{−n}f(u) du. Hence the bound of step 8 equals (2/(5r_0))∫_{5s'}^{5r_0} u^{−n}f(u) du.
10. As s ≤ s' ≤ 5s' and u^{−n}f(u) ≥ 0 for u > 0, ∫_{5s'}^{5r_0} u^{−n}f(u) du ≤ ∫_s^{r_0} u^{−n}f(u) du + ∫_{r_0}^{5r_0} u^{−n}f(u) du. Assume (i) for all ζ ∈ E and 0 < s ≤ r: s^{−n}∫_{B_s(ζ)} g dμ ≤ r^{−n}∫_{B_r(ζ)} g dμ + ∫_{(s,r]} τ^{−n}(∫_{B_τ(ζ)} φ dμ) dτ; and (ii) for μ-a.e. ζ with g(ζ) ≥ 1 there is t ≥ 1 with μ(B_ρ(ζ))/(ω_nρⁿ) → t as ρ ↓ 0. Then ∫_{{g ≥ 1}} g dμ ≤ 5ⁿ ω_n^{−1/n} (∫ g dμ)^{1/n} ∫ φ dμ.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra (a separable metric space); B_ρ(ζ) = closedBall ζ ρ; ω_n = omega n ∈ (0, ∞) (Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ: open, nonempty, bounded); μ(S) is read as a real number via Measure.real where it appears in quotients; all ∫ are Bochner integrals. Source: Steps 3 (good balls, Simon 5.7(1)) and 4 (covering, Simon Ch. 1, 3.4) of the parent proof, stated for an abstract measure μ (in the parent, μ = μ_V and φ = |∇^M g| + g|H|).

1. (Preliminaries.) g is μ-integrable (continuous with compact support, μ finite on compact sets), so Γ := ∫ g dμ ≥ 0 is finite and every ∫_S g dμ, ∫_S φ dμ is finite and nonnegative. Every closed ball is compact, so μ(B_ρ(ζ)) < ∞. Put F := ω_n^{−1}Γ ≥ 0, R := 2F^{1/n} and K := 5ⁿF^{1/n}. Since ω_n^{−1} ≥ 0 and Γ ≥ 0, F^{1/n} = (ω_n^{−1})^{1/n}Γ^{1/n} = ω_n^{−1/n}Γ^{1/n} (Real.mul_rpow, Real.inv_rpow, Real.rpow_neg), so K = 5ⁿω_n^{−1/n}(∫g dμ)^{1/n}, the constant in the claim; K ≥ 0.
2. (Good radius at a good point.) Let ζ ∈ E with g(ζ) ≥ 1 and t ≥ 1 such that μ(B_ρ(ζ))/(ω_nρⁿ) → t as ρ ↓ 0. For τ ∈ ℝ define f(τ) := ω_n^{−1}∫_{B_τ(ζ)} g dμ and k(τ) := ω_n^{−1}∫_{B_τ(ζ)} φ dμ. We verify the hypotheses of the sibling sobolev_good_radius_calculus with this F:
 (a) f and k are nondecreasing on (0, ∞): for 0 < τ ≤ τ', B_τ(ζ) ⊆ B_{τ'}(ζ) and g, φ are nonnegative and integrable.
 (b) For τ > 0: 0 ≤ f(τ) ≤ ω_n^{−1}∫ g dμ = F (g ≥ 0 integrable) and 0 ≤ k(τ).
 (c) The finite-interval inequality: for 0 < s ≤ r, multiply hypothesis (i) at ζ by ω_n^{−1} > 0; since ω_n^{−1}∫_{(s,r]} Ψ = ∫_{(s,r]} ω_n^{−1}Ψ for every Ψ, this is f(s)/sⁿ ≤ f(r)/rⁿ + ∫_{(s,r]} k(τ)/τⁿ dτ.
 (d) The lower density condition: let η < 1. If η < 0, then f(s)/sⁿ ≥ 0 > η for all s > 0. If 0 ≤ η < 1, put η_1 := (1 + η)/2, so η < η_1 < 1 and η/η_1 < 1. Since g is continuous at ζ and g(ζ) ≥ 1 > η_1, there is δ > 0 with g ≥ η_1 on B_δ(ζ); for 0 < s < δ, ∫_{B_s(ζ)} g dμ ≥ η_1μ(B_s(ζ)) (as μ(B_s(ζ)) < ∞), hence f(s)/sⁿ ≥ η_1·μ(B_s(ζ))/(ω_nsⁿ). Because μ(B_s(ζ))/(ω_nsⁿ) → t ≥ 1 > η/η_1, eventually as s ↓ 0 we have μ(B_s(ζ))/(ω_nsⁿ) > η/η_1, hence f(s)/sⁿ > η.  (2.1) ∫_{B_{5r_ζ}(ζ)} g dμ ≤ K ∫_{B_{r_ζ}(ζ)} φ dμ, with 0 < r_ζ < R.
3. (Removing the exceptional set.) Let Z := {ζ : g(ζ) ≥ 1 and there is no t ≥ 1 with μ(B_ρ(ζ))/(ω_nρⁿ) → t}. By hypothesis (ii), μ(Z) = 0; choose a Borel set N ⊇ Z with μ(N) = 0 (Mathlib exists_measurable_superset_of_null). The set {g ≥ 1} is closed (g continuous), so A := {g ≥ 1} ∖ N is Borel, and every ζ ∈ A satisfies the assumptions of step 2; fix such radii r_ζ for ζ ∈ A (choice). 4. (Covering.) As a ∈ B_{r_a}(a), A ⊆ ⋃_{b∈D} B_{5r_b}(b). D is countable: the balls B_{r_b}(b) are pairwise disjoint, each has nonempty interior (it contains the open ball of radius r_b > 0), and E is separable (Mathlib Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior).
5. (Summation.) Let ν_g(S) := ∫_S g dμ and ν_φ(S) := ∫_S φ dμ (finite Borel measures, as g, φ ≥ 0 are integrable; equivalently work with lower Lebesgue integrals of ofReal g, ofReal φ). Then

(Library pointer: steps 3–5 are, in lower-integral form, the axiom-clean SimonGMT lemma Chapter04.lintegral_le_of_ae_exists_good_radius applied to ofReal∘g, ofReal∘φ, the Borel set {g ≥ 1}, the radius bound R and the constant ofReal K, whose hypothesis is (2.1) for μ-a.e. ζ ∈ {g ≥ 1}; converting back uses ofReal(∫_S u dμ) = ∫⁻_S ofReal∘u dμ for integrable u ≥ 0.) ∎

This gives r_ζ < R = 2F^{1/n} with ∫_{B_{5r_ζ}(ζ)} g ≤ 5ⁿω_n^{−1/n}(∫g)^{1/n}∫_{B_{r_ζ}(ζ)} φ

Conventions. Source: Step 1, inequality (5.5), of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, 5.1–5.5; because g has compact support in U, 5.5 holds for all radii). subproblem.title: From the superlevel inequality (4.1) to the Sobolev inequality (truncation, layer cake, ε ↓ 0)
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 2, ℓ ∈ ℕ, V a rectifiable n-varifold in E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with μ = μ_V finite on compact sets and x ↦ p_{T_xV} μ-a.e. strongly measurable, U ⊆ E open, H: E → E locally μ-integrable on U, and C ≥ 0. Suppose that every g ∈ C¹(U), g ≥ 0, with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ U satisfies ∫_{{g≥1}} g dμ ≤ C(∫g dμ)^{1/n}∫(|∇^M g| + g|H|) dμ. Then every h ∈ C¹(U), h ≥ 0, with compact support and tsupport h ⊆ U satisfies (∫h^{n/(n−1)} dμ)^{(n−1)/n} ≤ (n/(n − 1))·C·∫(|∇^M h| + h|H|) dμ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (H : Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (h : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (C : ℝ), 2 ≤ n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight → IsOpen U → LocallyIntegrableOn H U V.weight → 0 ≤ C → (∀ g : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g U → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ U → (∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) → ∫ x in {x | 1 ≤ g x}, g x ∂V.weight ≤ C * (∫ x, g x ∂V.weight) ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∫ x, (‖V.tangentialGradient g x‖ + g x * ‖H x‖) ∂V.weight) → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 h U → HasCompactSupport h → tsupport h ⊆ U → (∀ x, 0 ≤ h x) → (∫ x, h x ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1)) ∂V.weight) ^ (((n : ℝ) - 1) / n) ≤ (n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1) * C * ∫ x, (‖V.tangentialGradient h x‖ + h x * ‖H x‖) ∂V.weight
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; B_ρ(ξ) = closedBall ξ ρ (closed ball); ω_n = omega n ∈ (0, ∞) for n ≥ 1 (Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ, which is open, nonempty and bounded); μ = μ_V = V.weight; p_x = (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection, the orthogonal projection onto T_xV, a continuous linear map with |p_x v| ≤ |v| (Mathlib Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le); ∇g(x) = gradient g x (0 where g is not differentiable); ∇^M g(x) = V.tangentialGradient g x = p_x(∇g(x)). All integrals ∫ are Bochner integrals (value 0 for non-integrable integrands), so integrability is checked wherever integrals are compared or split; ∫_{(a,b]} denotes the Lebesgue integral over the interval Ioc a b. Source: Steps 5 (truncation and layer cake) and 6 (ε ↓ 0) of the parent proof (end of the proof of Simon 5.7, with 4.11). Put p := n/(n − 1) (so p > 1, p − 1 = 1/(n − 1), 1/p = (n − 1)/n), K := tsupport h, M_s := {x : h(x) > s} for s ∈ ℝ, J := ∫(|∇^M h| + h|H|) dμ, Q := ∫ h^p dμ.

1. (Setup.) By the sibling sobolev_energy_integrable applied to h: h ∈ C¹(E), ∇^M h = 0 off K, and |∇^M h|, h|H| are μ-integrable; in particular J ≥ 0 is finite. K is compact with μ(K) < ∞; h is continuous, so every M_s is open (Borel), and for s ≥ 0, M_s ⊆ support h ⊆ K, so μ(M_s) < ∞. |H| is μ-integrable on K (local integrability on U, K ⊆ U compact). h^p is continuous, vanishes off K and is bounded, so Q < ∞.
2. (Cut-off.) Fix ε ∈ (0, 1] and let ψ(s) := smoothTransition(s/ε) (Mathlib Real.smoothTransition): ψ ∈ C^∞(ℝ), ψ is nondecreasing, 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 0 on (−∞, 0] and ψ = 1 on [ε, ∞). Hence ψ' ≥ 0 is continuous and bounded, and ψ' = 0 on (−∞, 0). (This ψ is the axiom-clean SimonGMT Chapter04.exists_smooth_superlevel_cutoff.)
3. (Truncations.) For t ≥ 0 let h_t := ψ ∘ (h − t). Then h_t ∈ C¹(E), so h_t is C¹ on U; 0 ≤ h_t ≤ 1; if h_t(x) ≠ 0 then h(x) − t > 0, so h(x) > t ≥ 0 and x ∈ support h; hence tsupport h_t ⊆ K ⊆ U and h_t has compact support. Moreover h_t ≤ 1_{M_t}, and h_t = 1 on M_{t+ε} (there h − t > ε), so M_{t+ε} ⊆ {h_t ≥ 1}. By the chain rule ∇h_t(x) = ψ'(h(x) − t)∇h(x), and p_x is linear, so ∇^M h_t(x) = ψ'(h(x) − t)∇^M h(x) and |∇^M h_t| = ψ'(h − t)|∇^M h| for every x.
4. (Truncated inequality.) Apply the hypothesis (4.1) to g := h_t (admissible by step 3). Left side: h_t ≥ 0 is integrable, M_{t+ε} ⊆ {h_t ≥ 1} and h_t = 1 on M_{t+ε}, so ∫_{{h_t ≥ 1}} h_t dμ ≥ ∫_{M_{t+ε}} h_t dμ = μ(M_{t+ε}). Right side: 0 ≤ ∫ h_t dμ ≤ μ(M_t), so (∫h_t dμ)^{1/n} ≤ μ(M_t)^{1/n}; and, the integrands being integrable (sibling sobolev_energy_integrable for h_t, or the bounds ψ'(h − t)|∇^M h| ≤ (sup ψ')|∇^M h| and h_t|H| ≤ 1_K|H|), ∫(|∇^M h_t| + h_t|H|) dμ = P(t) + ∫ h_t|H| dμ ≤ P(t) + R(t), where P(t) := ∫ ψ'(h − t)|∇^M h| dμ ≥ 0 and R(t) := ∫_{M_t} |H| dμ ≥ 0 (h_t|H| ≤ 1_{M_t}|H|). Since C ≥ 0:
 (4.a) μ(M_{t+ε}) ≤ C μ(M_t)^{1/n}(P(t) + R(t)) for every t ≥ 0.
5. (Moment factor.) Q_ε := ∫_{M_0}(h + ε)^p dμ < ∞ (bounded integrand, M_0 ⊆ K). For t ≥ 0, on M_t we have h + ε > t + ε ≥ 0, and M_t ⊆ M_0, so (t + ε)^p μ(M_t) ≤ ∫_{M_t}(h + ε)^p dμ ≤ Q_ε. Taking 1/n-th powers ((t + ε)^{p/n} = (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)}): (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)}μ(M_t)^{1/n} ≤ Q_ε^{1/n}. Multiplying (4.a) by (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)} ≥ 0:
 (5.a) (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)} μ(M_{t+ε}) ≤ C Q_ε^{1/n}(P(t) + R(t)) for every t ≥ 0.
6. (Integration in t, Tonelli; Simon 4.11.) All quantities are nonnegative; (x, t) ↦ ψ'(h(x) − t)|∇^M h(x)| and (x, t) ↦ 1_{h(x)>t}|H(x)| are (a.e.) measurable for μ ⊗ dt (continuous functions of (x, t) times a.e.-measurable functions of x), μ is σ-finite (finite on compacts in the σ-compact E), and t ↦ μ(M_{t+ε}) is nonincreasing, hence measurable. Integrate (5.a) over t ∈ (0, ∞) (as lower Lebesgue integrals of nonnegative functions):
 Left side: by the translation u = t + ε and Tonelli, ∫_0^∞ (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)}μ(M_{t+ε}) dt = ∫_ε^∞ u^{1/(n−1)}μ(M_u) du = ∫ (∫_ε^∞ u^{1/(n−1)}1_{h(x)>u} du) dμ(x) = ((n − 1)/n)∫_{M_ε}(h^p − ε^p) dμ, since for h(x) > ε the inner integral is ∫_ε^{h(x)} u^{1/(n−1)} du = ((n − 1)/n)(h(x)^p − ε^p), and it is 0 otherwise.
 Right side: by Tonelli, ∫_0^∞ P(t) dt = ∫ |∇^M h(x)| (∫_0^∞ ψ'(h(x) − t) dt) dμ(x), and for a := h(x) ≥ 0, ψ'(a − t) = 0 for t > a, so ∫_0^∞ ψ'(a − t) dt = ∫_0^a ψ'(a − t) dt = ψ(a) − ψ(0) = ψ(a) ≤ 1 (fundamental theorem of calculus); hence ∫_0^∞ P(t) dt ≤ ∫|∇^M h| dμ. Likewise ∫_0^∞ R(t) dt = ∫ |H(x)|(∫_0^∞ 1_{h(x)>t} dt) dμ(x) = ∫ h|H| dμ.
 Hence (6.a) ((n − 1)/n)∫_{M_ε}(h^p − ε^p) dμ ≤ C Q_ε^{1/n} J for every ε ∈ (0, 1]. (Library pointers, all axiom-clean: the Tonelli bound for ∫_0^∞(P + R) is SimonGMT Chapter04.lintegral_smooth_truncation_energy_le applied to μ⌞K; the layer-cake identities are Mathlib lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul / lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul.)
7. (ε ↓ 0.) Take ε = 1/k, k → ∞. Pointwise, 1_{M_ε}(h^p − ε^p) → h^p (if h(x) > 0 then eventually h(x) > ε and ε^p → 0; if h(x) = 0 both sides vanish), and 0 ≤ 1_{M_ε}(h^p − ε^p) ≤ h^p ≤ (max h)^p 1_K ∈ L¹(μ); by dominated convergence ∫_{M_ε}(h^p − ε^p) dμ → Q. Similarly 1_{M_0}(h + ε)^p → 1_{M_0}h^p with domination by (max h + 1)^p 1_K, so Q_ε → ∫_{M_0}h^p dμ = Q (h^p = 0 off M_0). As y ↦ y^{1/n} is continuous on [0, ∞), Q_ε^{1/n} → Q^{1/n}. Letting k → ∞ in (6.a): ((n − 1)/n)Q ≤ C Q^{1/n} J.
8. (Conclusion.) If Q = 0, the left side of the claim is 0^{(n−1)/n} = 0 ≤ (n/(n − 1))·C·J because C ≥ 0 and J ≥ 0. If Q > 0, divide step 7 by ((n − 1)/n)Q^{1/n} > 0: Q^{(n−1)/n} = Q^{1−1/n} = Q/Q^{1/n} ≤ (n/(n − 1))·C·J. This is (∫h^{n/(n−1)} dμ)^{(n−1)/n} ≤ (n/(n − 1))·C·∫(|∇^M h| + h|H|) dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Truncations h_t = ψ(h − t) with a C¹ cut-off ψ (0 on (−∞,0], 1 on [ε,∞)) are admissible, h_t = 1 on {h > t+ε}, h_t ≤ 1_{h>t}, |∇^M h_t| = ψ'(h − t)|∇^M h|
The hypothesis for h_t gives μ(M_{t+ε}) ≤ Cμ(M_t)^{1/n}[∫ψ'(h−t)|∇^M h| + ∫_{M_t}|H|]
Multiply by (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)} and use (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)}μ(M_t)^{1/n} ≤ Q_ε^{1/n}
Integrate in t (Tonelli, layer cake): ((n−1)/n)∫_{M_ε}(h^p − ε^p) ≤ CQ_ε^{1/n}∫(|∇^M h| + h|H|)
Let ε ↓ 0 by dominated convergence and divide by Q^{1/n} (Q = 0 trivial)
